content: 1. When using cabozantinib capsules, reduce the dose by 40 mg (e.g., from 140 mg/day to 100 mg/day or from 100 mg/day to 60 mg/day). Resume the cabozantinib dose that was used prior to initiating mifepristone treatment 2 to 3 days after discontinuing mifepristone. 2. Mifepristone increases the levels or effects of calcifediol by inhibiting hepatic and intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. 3. Mifepristone increases the levels or effects of cannabidiol by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Adjust therapy and monitor closely. Consider reducing the cannabidiol dose when co-administered with a strong CYP3A4 inhibitor. 4. Carbamazepine may decrease mifepristone levels via CYP3A4 induction. Conversely, mifepristone may increase carbamazepine levels by inhibiting CYP2C8/2C9. Use caution and monitor closely. 5. Cenobamate decreases mifepristone levels or effects by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Adjust therapy and monitor closely. Increase the dose of the CYP3A4 substrate as needed when co-administered with cenobamate. 6. Mifepristone increases ceritinib levels by inhibiting the P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporter. Both drugs may increase each other's toxicity by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. Monitor closely and modify therapy as needed. This combination may also increase the risk of QT prolongation. 7. Mifepristone increases the levels or effects of chloroquine by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Adjust therapy and monitor closely. 8. Mifepristone and chlorpromazine both prolong the QTc interval. Monitor closely and modify therapy as needed. Use alternative medications if available. 9. Mifepristone increases the toxicity of cholic acid by reducing its elimination. Avoid concomitant use of bile salt efflux pump (BSEP) inhibitors, as this may exacerbate the accumulation of conjugated bile salts in the liver, leading to clinical symptoms. If co-administration is necessary, monitor serum transaminases and bilirubin levels. 10. Mifepristone increases the levels or effects of inhaled ciclesonide by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. 11. Ciprofloxacin increases mifepristone levels or effects by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Adjust therapy and monitor closely. Use alternative medications if available. 12. Mifepristone and citalopram both prolong the QTc interval. Monitor closely and modify therapy as needed. If concurrent therapy is essential, ECG monitoring is recommended. 13. Clarithromycin increases mifepristone levels or effects by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Do not exceed 300 mg/day of mifepristone for Cushing syndrome when co-administered with strong CYP3A4 inhibitors. This combination may also prolong the QT interval. Use alternative medications if available. 14. Mifepristone and clomipramine both prolong the QTc interval. Monitor closely and modify therapy as needed. Use alternative medications if available. 15. Mifepristone increases clonazepam levels or effects by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. 16. Mifepristone and clozapine both prolong the QTc interval. Monitor closely and modify therapy as needed. Use alternative medications if available. 17. Cobicistat increases mifepristone levels or effects by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. If co-administration is necessary, administer an initial dose of 300 mg mifepristone and do not exceed 600 mg. Adjust the mifepristone dose based on the patient's current regimen. For example, if cobicistat is initiated in a patient receiving 600 mg mifepristone, reduce the dose to 300 mg. If the patient is already on 300 mg mifepristone, no dose adjustment is necessary. 18. Mifepristone increases cobimetinib levels or effects by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. For short-term co-administration (14 days or less), reduce the cobimetinib dose to 20 mg once daily for patients normally taking 60 mg daily. After discontinuing mifepristone, resume cobimetinib at the previous dose. Use alternatives to mifepristone in patients already taking a reduced dose of cobimetinib (20–40 mg daily). 19. Conivaptan increases mifepristone levels or effects by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Do not exceed 300 mg/day of mifepristone for Cushing syndrome when co-administered with strong CYP3A4 inhibitors. 20. Mifepristone increases conjugated estrogen levels or effects by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely.
